findings.desc: doc-promise-undelivered: packages/main/src/handlers/finding-runtime-evidence.ts:1-12 claims a Finding-owned two-command runtime-evidence handler facade, but line 7 aliases createFindingLedgerHandlers wholesale; that factory also returns finding_ledger_query, while the facade itself is consumed only by the immutable RED test and is not wired by packages/main/src/registry.ts or exported by packages/main/src/index.ts/package exports. The acknowledged expansion therefore does not establish the promised narrow/public runtime command boundary and can leak Ledger Query responsibility if later registered. Replace the alias with a narrow wrapper that returns exactly finding_runtime_evidence_run and finding_runtime_evidence_verify and wire/export the intended boundary, or remove the public-boundary promise/expansion with proof that the direct registered ledger handler is the canonical contract.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by cea6f401 and subsequent facade registration: finding_runtime_evidence_run/verify are wired through createFindingRuntimeEvidenceHandlers, and fresh mechanical selectors runtime.real_cli_run_adapter, runtime.real_cli_verify_adapter, runtime.registered_key_trust, and runtime.carrier_trust_chain all pass on current storyFilesHash.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/handlers/finding.ts:569 display-ID allocation still uses findings.length + 1, so a sparse legacy set such as F-001/F-003 allocates F-003 again; lines 632-634 then find the old row by display ID and neither replace nor append when recordId differs, silently hiding the newly durable ledger record from readFindings. This preserves the historical ID-reuse/vanishing-row failure despite globally unique recordIds.
